name: tpr-research
description: Research the Pāḷi Tipiṭaka, commentaries and translations in your Tipitaka Pali Reader, and make papers and reports with quotes and links that open TPR.
long_description:
TPR Research lets Claude read the books in your Tipitaka Pali Reader (TPR): the Pāḷi canon, the Aṭṭhakathā and Ṭīkā, later handbooks, and the translations you have installed.

Ask a question such as *"Where do the suttas mention the heart-base? Show me with quotes"* and Claude searches TPR's own index, counts occurrences, reads each passage in context with its commentary, and writes a paper: Pāḷi quotes in grey boxes, the English under each, and a link that opens TPR on the right page. It also makes reports from your own TPR: what you have been reading, a vocabulary review of the words you looked up, a sutta or chapter exported as a Pāḷi page with the translation, and word studies. Papers and reports are saved as Markdown, HTML and PDF in the TPR folder in your home folder.

TPR's files are only read, never changed. You need Tipitaka Pali Reader, opened once so it finishes setting up, with at least one search run so its index is built. Install the English translation in TPR (Settings → Download) for English under the quotes.

On a Mac, the first time Claude reads TPR's data macOS asks whether Claude may access another app's data. Allow it: the extension opens every database read-only.

papers_dir.title: Folder for papers
papers_dir.description: Where finished papers and reports are saved.

tpr_data_dir.title: TPR data folder (optional)
tpr_data_dir.description: Leave empty: it is found automatically. Set it only if TPR is installed somewhere unusual. It is the folder holding tipitaka_pali.db.

tools.name: tpr_research_guide
tools.description: How to research with these tools, and the paper format

tools.name: tpr_status
tools.description: Check the TPR data folder, search index and translations

tools.name: tpr_books
tools.description: List book ids, layers and names

tools.name: tpr_search
tools.description: Search the Pāḷi or a translation with TPR's own index

tools.name: tpr_count
tools.description: Count occurrences per book and layer, to prove presence or absence

tools.name: tpr_show
tools.description: Show a passage with its translation, line by line

tools.name: tpr_quote
tools.description: A ready quote: bold Pāḷi, translation and TPR link

tools.name: tpr_link
tools.description: The TPR link and page for a line

tools.name: tpr_commentary
tools.description: Commentary passages TPR links to a paragraph

tools.name: tpr_query
tools.description: A read-only SQL query on the books, for what the other tools cannot find

tools.name: tpr_lookup
tools.description: Grammar and dictionary entries for a Pāḷi word

tools.name: tpr_activity
tools.description: What you recently opened, searched and looked up in TPR

tools.name: tpr_vocabulary
tools.description: The words you looked up, with meanings and where you met them

tools.name: tpr_chapters
tools.description: The headings of a book, with where each starts

tools.name: tpr_export
tools.description: A sutta, chapter or book as Pāḷi with the translation

tools.name: tpr_save_paper
tools.description: Save a paper or report as Markdown, HTML and PDF, and open it

prompts.name: research_paper
prompts.description: Research a question in your TPR library and write a paper with Pāḷi quotes and TPR links
prompts.text: Call tpr_research_guide first and follow it. Then research this in my Tipitaka Pali Reader with the TPR Research tools (not files on disk), write the paper with Pāḷi quotes and TPR links, and save it with tpr_save_paper: ${arguments.question}

prompts.name: reading_report
prompts.description: A report of what you have been reading, searching and looking up in TPR
prompts.text: Call tpr_research_guide first and follow its Reports section. Then make my TPR reading report with tpr_activity (days back: ${arguments.days}; 30 if empty) and save it with tpr_save_paper.

prompts.name: vocabulary_review
prompts.description: The Pāḷi words you looked up in TPR, with meanings and where you met them
prompts.text: Call tpr_research_guide first and follow its Reports section. Then make my vocabulary review with tpr_vocabulary (days back: ${arguments.days}; 30 if empty) and save it with tpr_save_paper.

prompts.name: export_text
prompts.description: A sutta, chapter or book as a Pāḷi page with the translation
prompts.text: Call tpr_research_guide first. Then export ${arguments.what} from my TPR with tpr_books, tpr_chapters and tpr_export, and save it unchanged with tpr_save_paper.

prompts.name: word_study
prompts.description: One Pāḷi word through the dictionaries, the canon and the commentaries
prompts.text: Call tpr_research_guide first and follow its Reports section. Then make a word study of ${arguments.word} with the TPR Research tools and save it with tpr_save_paper.
